findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the committed request/response evidence MUST be credential-scrubbed (redact Authorization/PAT headers, Cookie/Set-Cookie, and any token bodies) before it is landed, and make the scrub a required step of the artifact-emission path rather than a reviewer's manual duty.
evidence: Plan: 'producing a committed artifact — the declared capability contract plus the raw request/response evidence behind it — which a human reviews and lands'
Plan: 'Every answer must carry its raw request and response.'
Plan: 'The job holds an admin PAT on a throwaway instance' — admin-authenticated calls attach an Authorization/PAT header to every request; responses to auth flows can carry Set-Cookie/session tokens
T10(e): 'no plaintext secrets in IaC/vars'; a plaintext secret on a committed path is a MAJOR class
findings.finding: The plan mandates committing an artifact of 'raw request/response evidence' from admin-PAT-authenticated REST calls, but never requires scrubbing credentials from that evidence before it is committed. Raw requests carry the Authorization/PAT header and raw responses can carry Set-Cookie/session tokens, so the committed data can leak a live admin credential onto a permanent path.
findings.location: Plan sections 'The load-bearing constraint' (committed artifact = 'the declared capability contract plus the raw request/response evidence behind it') and 'Every answer must carry its raw request and response'; AC line 1 ('emitting a structured artifact (raw request/response per question)')
scenarios: The capability map records a POST /rest/pat/latest/tokens or an authenticated REST call verbatim; the request block includes the admin PAT / Authorization header, and it is reviewed-and-landed into the committed contract
A future re-pin regenerates the artifact and a reviewer commits it without noticing an embedded token
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the artifact spec: the emitter redacts Authorization/Cookie/Set-Cookie headers and known token fields in every captured request/response before writing the artifact, and a check (gitleaks or an assertion) fails if a token-shaped string survives into the committed contract.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC that the harness setup assertion (or the contract loader) verifies the contract's recorded image digest equals the harness's pinned digest and FAILS on mismatch, so a re-pin without a re-run of the mapping job is caught rather than silently consuming a stale contract.
evidence: 'the resulting environment contract is COMMITTED as data and consumed by the harness's setup assertion — it does NOT re-derive anything at test time'
'run again only when the image is re-pinned' names the update trigger but no mechanism enforces it
'Pin by digest in this job too, or the map describes an image we do not run' addresses the producer digest but not the consumer's staleness check
findings.finding: The committed environment contract is shared state consumed by the harness setup assertion, but the plan does not specify an assertion binding the contract's recorded image digest to the digest the harness actually runs — so a re-pin without a re-run leaves the harness silently consuming a stale contract describing a different image.
findings.location: Acceptance criteria (AC4) and 'Caveats' ('Pin by digest in this job too')
scenarios: Operator re-pins the DC image digest but forgets to re-run the mapping job; the harness setup assertion reads the stale contract and passes against field ids / template facts that no longer hold for the running image.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the image digest inside the committed contract and have the setup assertion compare it to the harness's pinned digest, failing with a 're-run the mapping job for the new digest' message on mismatch.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify why the fixed checklist needs an LLM agent rather than a deterministic REST script (as jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml already does), or scope the LLM to only genuinely open-ended follow-up while the enumerated probes and their present/absent/different verdicts are computed deterministically from raw responses.
evidence: Plan: 'This should answer specific questions and emit structured results' — the questions are fully enumerated (inventory + fixed experiments + the 37e7/1a9f falsifiers), i.e. a closed set, not open-ended.
Plan: 'otherwise we have swapped "discovering from the instance" for "trusting a model", which is worse' — the plan's own stated hazard is exactly what an LLM in the loop reintroduces.
Codebase: .github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml + scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py answer the same class of DC question with 'plain deterministic urllib: no LLM, no agent'.
Codebase: scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py's REST layer (_raw_request) is stdlib urllib; the LLM only orchestrates/summarizes the fixed calls.

Codebase: follow-up ticket a9bd-6641-e603-42bc was filed because the LLM-summarised answers were WRONG at an unchanged digest (two retracted claims in docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md), a failure a deterministic pass avoids.
findings.finding: The plan mandates an LLM/Opus agent to answer what it itself specifies as a closed, enumerable checklist of fixed REST probes with deterministic verdicts (present/absent/present-but-different); a deterministic script (the pattern already used by the sibling jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml) would answer the same questions without putting a model between the raw evidence and the contract — which the plan's own 'do not trust a model' requirement argues for.
findings.location: Plan sections 'What it should answer — a CHECKLIST, not open-ended exploration' and 'Every answer must carry its raw request and response'
scenarios: A future re-pin dispatches the map; the agent mis-reads correct evidence.json and the committed contract records a claim that is false about the very image it maps — reproducing the retracted 254-char-label and duplicate-Task defects.
Cost/non-determinism: a billable Opus run with a 900-step budget is spent to make REST calls whose shapes are already known and listed in the plan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the fallback for a failed/incomplete checklist sub-step: whether the run aborts and emits no contract, or records the sub-step as explicitly unanswered, and state that a partially-populated contract must not be landable/consumable as complete.
evidence: Plan: 'Boot time is minutes; batch every question into one run rather than iterating' — establishes a single run over many sub-steps but no per-sub-step failure handling
Absence rationale: the plan never states whether a failed question aborts the run, is recorded as unanswered, or is retried; nor whether a partially-populated artifact may be committed

Confirmation this was an undecided decision: the implementation had to invent a fallback — on LLMError it exits 1 and does NOT write capability_map.json, while always writing evidence.json and a run_metadata.json `run_succeeded` flag (scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py:595-613)
findings.finding: The plan specifies a single batched run over a minutes-long, multi-question checklist but gives no fallback protocol for an incomplete or failed sub-step (a probe erroring, template creation failing, or a partial boot).
findings.location: Section 'Caveats worth designing against' ('Boot time is minutes; batch every question into one run') and AC line 1
scenarios: One experiment (e.g. POST issuetype) errors midway; the agent emits a contract with that answer missing, and a human lands a half-complete contract that the setup assertion then trusts
A transient boot/probe failure yields a contract that silently omits the Epic-Link screen question
findings.suggested_fix: State that any unanswerable question must be recorded with an explicit `unanswered`/`error` verdict carrying the raw failure, and that the artifact is marked not-complete (blocking the human land / setup consumption) unless every checklist question resolved.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a positive rationale for using an LLM/agentic runtime to run this fixed checklist (e.g. adaptive endpoint discovery) OR adopt a deterministic checklist script (raw REST, no model in the loop) that emits the same structured answers + raw request/response evidence, since the enumerated questions require no model reasoning and the plan itself names 'an LLM in the loop' as the risk to avoid.
evidence: The plan's own load-bearing constraint warns the failure mode is 'more non-determinism and an LLM in the loop' and insists 'the deliverable is committed DATA, not a running agent'
The plan frames the work as 'a CHECKLIST, not open-ended exploration' and 'This should answer specific questions and emit structured results' — i.e. a fixed sequence of REST calls

'Every answer must carry its raw request and response' — a deterministic script produces this trivially and traceably; an agent adds a summarization layer the plan itself distrusts ('trusting a model, which is worse')
ABSENCE: no sentence gives a reason the checklist REQUIRES an agent (e.g. discovering unknown endpoints, adaptive branching) rather than a deterministic runner
findings.finding: The plan chooses an LLM/agentic runtime to execute a fully-enumerated, mechanical checklist, but states no positive rationale for that choice over a deterministic script — and the checklist as written (GET templates, GET /rest/api/2/field, POST /rest/api/2/issuetype, read editmeta back, two raw falsifier PUTs) is a closed, non-exploratory set of REST calls that needs no model reasoning to execute.
findings.location: Sections 'What it should answer — a CHECKLIST, not open-ended exploration' and AC1
scenarios: A future re-pin run where the model paraphrases or omits a field id, or takes a non-deterministic path through the checklist, reintroducing exactly the model-trust risk the plan argues against
Reviewer of the committed contract cannot easily diff a model-authored artifact run-to-run because the agent's tool-call order and phrasing vary
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence justifying the agentic choice against a plain script, or specify the deliverable as a deterministic mapping script whose output is the candidate contract; reserve any LLM use for genuinely open-ended follow-up questions the checklist cannot enumerate.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify running the mutating experiments and 37e7/1a9f falsifiers through the LLM agent rather than the established deterministic urllib probe pattern (`scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py`), or move those fixed-request/response checks to a deterministic probe.
evidence: scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py + .github/workflows/jira-dc-epic-link-probe.yml are 'plain deterministic urllib, no LLM, no agent, four predetermined REST calls' answering only narrow questions.

That workflow's header explicitly argues the agentic map should NOT be re-run to settle narrow deterministic questions ('slow, billable, and would risk churning answers that are already reviewed and landed').

The plan's own principle 'Every answer must carry its raw request and response ... otherwise we have swapped discovering from the instance for trusting a model, which is worse' points toward deterministic probes for the yes/no experiment questions.
findings.finding: The plan routes the mutating 'experiments' (POST /rest/api/2/issuetype, add-field-to-screen, the two falsifier PUTs) through the LLM authoring agent, without justifying that over the cheaper deterministic (non-LLM) probe pattern already established in the repo for narrow, targeted platform questions.
findings.location: Plan section 'Experiments (validate the configuration hooks BEFORE we depend on them)'
scenarios: The falsifier / hook-validation questions (deterministic, fixed request/response) are answered by a non-deterministic LLM pass when a plain-urllib probe would be cheaper and more reproducible.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the environment-contract artifact's file path and schema (which fields carry the template->Epic mapping, field ids, screen presence booleans, and per-question raw request/response) and name the harness setup-assertion file that consumes it.

AC4: 'the resulting environment contract is COMMITTED as data and consumed by the harness's setup assertion'
No file path or schema for the contract; no location for the setup assertion that consumes it
findings.finding: The 'structured artifact' / 'environment contract' committed data has no specified schema or file path, and the consuming 'harness setup assertion' has no named location — yet AC4 requires the harness to consume it deterministically.
scenarios: Executor authors the artifact in an ad-hoc shape the harness assertion can't parse

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the concrete assertion for AC5 (e.g. a CI/lint check that parses the workflow YAML and fails if any `on:` key other than `workflow_dispatch` is present) as the proving command.
evidence: AC5: 'the workflow cannot run on push, PR, or schedule, and this is asserted, not merely configured'
No described check/command that would produce evidence the workflow lacks those triggers
findings.finding: AC5 requires the trigger restriction be 'asserted, not merely configured' but the plan describes no concrete proving mechanism for asserting the ABSENCE of push/PR/schedule triggers.
scenarios: Executor edits the YAML to workflow_dispatch-only but adds no test, satisfying 'configured' but not the 'asserted' clause AC5 explicitly demands
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test that loads the workflow YAML and asserts `set(workflow['on'].keys()) == {'workflow_dispatch'}`, run in the harness CI.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve who records the 37e7/1a9f falsifier raw responses onto those tickets: state that the committed artifact carries the falsifier request/response verbatim and a HUMAN transcribes/links it during review, keeping the agent's report-not-mutate / touch-nothing-outside-the-instance constraint intact.
evidence: AC3: 'the 37e7 and 1a9f falsifiers are executed and their raw responses recorded on those tickets'
Caveat: 'it must touch nothing outside it' and 'The agent must be told to REPORT rather than FIX'

The declared deliverable is 'a committed artifact ... which a human reviews and lands' — implying human, not agent, transacts anything durable outside the container, but this is never made explicit for the ticket-recording step
findings.finding: AC3 requires the 37e7 and 1a9f falsifiers' raw responses to be 'recorded ON THOSE TICKETS', but the plan's load-bearing constraint forbids the agent from touching anything outside the throwaway instance and mandates it 'REPORT rather than FIX'. The plan never says who performs the on-ticket recording (a human landing the reviewed artifact vs. the agent writing to the rebar ticket store), leaving the mechanism ambiguous at exactly the boundary it drew.
findings.location: AC3 vs. 'Caveats worth designing against' (agent must touch nothing outside the instance; REPORT not FIX)
scenarios: Implementer wires the agent to comment on rebar tickets to satisfy AC3, violating the report-not-mutate / touch-nothing-outside constraint
Implementer treats the recording as a human step but AC1's artifact does not carry the falsifier evidence in a form a reviewer can transcribe, so AC3 is unmet
findings.suggested_fix: Reword AC3 so the falsifier evidence is captured in the reviewed artifact and the on-ticket recording is a human review action, explicitly disallowing the agent from writing to the rebar ticket store.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the plan's relationship to the EXISTING capability-map machinery (`.github/workflows/jira-dc-capability-map.yml`, `scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py`, `docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md`, `tests/unit/test_jira_dc_capability_map_workflow.py`, ticket 259b-b7da-a346-4785): whether this plan is that already-landed work, an extension of it, or a replacement — and if extension/replacement, which specific ACs are not already satisfied by it.

scripts/jira_dc_capability_map.py docstring: 'an on-demand, `workflow_dispatch`-only CI job that boots the digest-pinned Jira DC harness ... so we DECLARE the DC environment contract instead of discovering it live ... docs/jira-dc-capability-map.md already documents the committed answers (Epic Link=customfield_10001, Epic Name=customfield_10003, screen presence, all three software templates yield Epic), the re-run-on-repin rule, and 'authored, not live' — satisfying the plan's last four ACs.

conftest.py _PROJECT_TEMPLATE/_REQUIRED_FIELDS + _assert_project_capabilities already consume the contract as committed data at setup without re-deriving at test time (plan AC4).

rebar:1a9f and rebar:37e7 record the falsifiers already executed with raw responses (req-0054..0058) by run 30863672922 — the plan's 'the 37e7 and 1a9f falsifiers are executed and their raw responses recorded' AC is already met.

findings.location: Whole plan; esp. 'Acceptance criteria' and 'Why this is the right instrument'
scenarios: An implementer picks up this plan and builds a second, parallel capability-mapping workflow/script/doc, creating two sources of truth about the DC environment contract.
Reviewer cannot tell whether the plan intends to REPLACE, EXTEND, or DUPLICATE jira-dc-capability-map.yml.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Prior art' section citing 259b-b7da-a346-4785 and its four committed artifacts, and re-scope the ACs to only the delta over what already exists (if any). If the intent is documentation of already-done work, mark it as such rather than as new build.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the admin PAT's provenance and lifetime: it should be minted in-process against the ephemeral instance for the single run (never supplied, committed, or persisted beyond the run), and state this explicitly in the caveat that calls it 'acceptable'.
evidence: Plan: 'The job holds an admin PAT on a throwaway instance — acceptable, but it must touch nothing outside it, and must not be reachable from a fork PR.'
T10(b): 'no long-lived credentials committed'; service-to-service credentials should be scoped and short-lived
The plan constrains the instance's blast radius but is silent on where the PAT comes from and how long it lives
findings.finding: The plan asserts the job 'holds an admin PAT' and calls that 'acceptable', but does not specify the PAT's provenance or storage discipline — whether it is an ephemeral token minted against the throwaway instance for the run, or a long-lived credential injected/stored — so the 'no long-lived credentials' least-privilege discipline is left unstated.
findings.location: Plan section 'Caveats worth designing against' ('The job holds an admin PAT on a throwaway instance — acceptable, but it must touch nothing outside it')
scenarios: An implementer supplies the admin PAT as a persisted repository/environment secret rather than minting an ephemeral token against the throwaway instance, creating a standing long-lived admin credential
Ambiguity leads a reviewer to accept a committed or externally-issued PAT because the plan only said 'acceptable'
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the caveat to read that the admin PAT is minted against the throwaway instance for the duration of the run and is never supplied from or stored in a persisted secret, matching the harness's existing self-minted-token approach.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the emitted capability-contract schema explicitly: the per-question record keys, how each raw request/response pair is keyed to its answer, and the closed verdict vocabulary each vocabulary/screen diff entry must carry (e.g. present | absent | present_but_different), co-located with the setup assertion that consumes it.
evidence: Plan: 'emitting a structured artifact (raw request/response per question)' and 'the resulting environment contract is COMMITTED as data and consumed by the harness's setup assertion'

The artifact is produced by an LLM ('an LLM in the loop', 'trusting a model') and consumed by a named downstream deterministic consumer (the setup assertion) — a structured-output contract, so its shape/enum is load-bearing

The plan enumerates QUESTIONS (which template yields Epic, Epic Link/Name field ids, screen presence, whether create-issue-type + edit-screen work) but never a record shape: per-question keys, how raw request/response pairs are associated with each answer, or the pass/fail verdict vocabulary each diff entry must carry

Confirmation the vocabulary is undefined-but-needed: the implementation had to invent an explicit verdict enum ('present', 'absent', 'present_but_different') and per-question field keys (falsifier_37e7_parent_editmeta, falsifier_1a9f_ac1_subtask_put_parent, epic_link_write_takes_effect) — none of which appear in the plan
findings.finding: The plan mandates an agent-emitted "structured artifact" / "declared capability contract" that the harness's setup assertion consumes, but never defines that structured-output contract's schema or its verdict value vocabulary.
findings.location: Section 'What it should answer', 'Every answer must carry its raw request and response', and AC lines 1-2 & 4
scenarios: The agent returns a differently-shaped or prose-ish object and the harness setup assertion cannot parse it, or parses it ambiguously (e.g. Epic-presence left implicit rather than an explicit verdict)
Two runs on two digests emit inconsistent key names, so the committed contract is not diffable across re-pins
findings.suggested_fix: In the AC or a dedicated 'Artifact schema' section, enumerate the required top-level keys and, for each checklist question, the answer field plus a required `verdict` drawn from a fixed enum, so the harness setup assertion reads named fields rather than interpreting prose.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State that the 'REPORT, do not FIX' and 'raw REST, no rebar transport in the path' constraints must be encoded in the agent's own instructions/prompt (not only in this ticket), so the executing agent is actually bound by them.
evidence: Plan: 'The agent must be told to REPORT rather than FIX' — names the constraint but not where the telling must occur (the prompt/instructions vs. only this ticket)
Plan: '[rebar:1a9f...] AC1 ... Raw REST, no rebar in the path' — a per-experiment constraint on the agent's tool use that is stated in the checklist prose but not tied to an instruction location
Instruction-locality concern: constraints an executor agent must honor need to live in the agent's own instructions; the plan leaves their placement implicit
findings.finding: The plan states the 'REPORT rather than FIX' and 'no rebar in the path' behavioral constraints only as prose caveats, without locating them in the agent's actual instructions/prompt.
findings.location: Section 'Caveats worth designing against' ('The agent must be told to REPORT rather than FIX') and 'Experiments' ('Raw REST, no rebar in the path')
scenarios: The agent, seeing a config gap it could 'fix', mutates the throwaway instance or proposes harness edits because the report-not-fix rule was never in its prompt
A falsifier is accidentally routed through a rebar transport, contaminating the raw-REST evidence the verdict depends on

evidence: Log title: 'close the capability-map staleness gap — derive the digest provenance instead of duplicating it'
Plan caveat: 'Pin by digest in this job too, or the map describes an image we do not run.'
Plan Inventory: 'exact image digest, Jira version, and licensed applications'
Plan AC: 're-run it (image re-pin)' — re-derivation on re-pin, but no single-source-of-truth for the digest across job + contract + harness
findings.finding: The log's central expressed decision — 'derive the digest provenance instead of duplicating it' — is not honored: the plan duplicates the pinned digest across the mapping job, the committed contract, and the harness image pin without any mechanism to derive one from a single source, which reintroduces the staleness/drift the ticket is meant to close.
scenarios: The harness image pin is bumped but the committed contract's recorded digest is not re-derived, so the contract silently describes a stale image — the exact staleness gap the ticket set out to close.
A reviewer sees three copies of the digest (job pin, contract data, harness pin) with no declared derivation relationship and cannot tell which is authoritative.
